title: SA/105/2003 of RAJENDRA DUTT KOTHARI Vs NATHI PRASAD KOTHARI and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 105 of 2003
Shri Rajendra Dutt Kothari ... Revisionist
vs.
 Shri Nathi Prasad Kothari & Others ... Respondent
Mr. S.K. Jain, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Siddhartha Jain and Mr. Balvinder Singh,
Advocates present for the appellant.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Pratul Kumar, Advocate present for
the respondents.
U. C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
1. A Recall Application being MCC No. 743/2013, supported
by an affidavit of Sri Rakesh Kumar, has been filed on behalf of
the appellants on 18.11.2013 with the following facts:
i. The deponent is son and legal heir and representative of
respondent no. 1 who died on 27.12.2008 leaving behind
him the deponent (son) and wife Smt. Bhagwati Devi.
ii. After the death of Late Nathi Prasad Kothari (respondent
no. 1) his legal heirs deponent and his wife Smt.
Bhagwati Devi (mother of deponent) have not been
impleaded in the Second Appeal No. 105/2003 and after
90 days of the death of Late Nathi Prasad Kothari the
aforesaid Second Appeal stands abated against the
respondent no. 1.
iii. The appellants/defendants are the residents of the same
village and cousin of the respondent no. 1 and were fully
aware of the death of deceased (Nathi Prasad Kothari)
respondent no. 1 and even than the applicants who are
legal heir and representatives of the deceased have not
been substituted.
iv. The respondent no. 1 Nathi Prasad Kothari has expired on
27.12.2008 leaving behind his wife Smt. Bhagwati Devi
and his son Rakesh Kumar, but after the death of Nathi
Prasad Kothari his aforesaid legal heirs and
representatives have not been impleaded and the appeal
has been decided without giving any opportunity to
them, therefore the impugned judgment and order dated
23.05.2013 is liable to be recalled.
v. After the death of Sri. Nathi Prasad Kothari (respondent
no. 10) on 27.12.2008 the Second Appeal against him
stand abated after 90 days of his death, therefore the
judgment and order could not have been passed in an
abated appeal.

-2-
vi. The judgment and order dated 23.05.2013 has been
passed against the dead person and therefore is liable to
be recalled.
vii. The Suit No. 377 of 1953 was filed by Kundan Lal for
partition in the Court of Civil Judge, Dehradun which
was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 21.05.1959
in which 2/3rd share of Kundan Lal was declared and
just 1/3rd share was found of defendant no. 1 Rajendra
Dutt Kothari. The final decree was passed in the said
Suit on 17.08.1963. The plaintiffs in Suit No. 54/1994
had sought a decree of injunction restraining the
defendants from selling the disputed property but the
Trial Court vide its judgment and decree dated
17.02.1995 dismissed the said suit, the judgment and
decree dated 17.10.1995 was reversed by the Appellate
Court vide his judgment dated 15.10.2003 in Civil
Appeal No. 95/1995 (Changed No. 06/1998) and the suit
filed on behalf of the plaintiffs/respondents was decreed.
While deciding the second appeal the Hon'ble High
Court erred in law in holding that the suit filed on behalf
of the plaintiff/respondents was not maintainable before
the Civil Court in view of Section 331 (Schedule II) of
U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act 1950, whereas the suit was only for
injunction.
viii. The deponent has received the certified copy of the
judgment and order dated 23.05.2013 from Sri. M.M.
Bhatt, Advocate Civil Court, Dehradun who received the
certified copy of the judgment and order communicated
to him by the counsel appearing on behalf of the
respondents before the Hon'ble High Court.
ix. Thereafter the deponent immediately came to Nainital
alongwith necessary documents and expenses on
24.10.2013 and contacted Mr. Tarun Lakhera, Advocate
High Court who prepared the recall application on
25/26.10.2013 and on 27th October was Sunday and
now it is being filed without any further delay.
x. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, it is
expedient in the interest of justice that this Hon'ble
Court may kindly be pleased to allow the aforesaid recall
application and recall the judgment and order dated
23.05.2013 passed by the Hon'ble P.C. Pant, in Second
Appeal No. 105/2003 "Rajendra Dutt Kothari and others
vs. Nathi Prasad Kothari and others".
2. The appellants have filed the objections to the said
application with an affidavit of one Sri. Ashok Kothari with the
following grounds:
(i) Sri. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate was representing the
plaintiffs/respondents and filed his Vakalatnama on
their behalf. In case the respondent no. 1 Nathi
Prasad Kothari was died on 27.12.2008 as alleged by
the applicants, it was the duty of the legal heirs of
deceased to move the application for implement in
place of deceased in the second appeal or it was the

-3-
duty of their counsel to inform the Court about the
date of death so that the court may be directed to the
appellant to take steps for deceased therefore, the
date of death of the deceased is seems to be
suspicious therefore, they cannot take the advantage
of their own negligence.
(ii) At the time of arguments in the second appeal, the
counsel of the respondents did not disclose about the
death of Nathi Prasad Kothari respondent no. 1 and
argued the case on behalf of all the respondents and
after heard the arguments of both the parties the
Hon'ble Court decided the appeal on merits and
allowed the same on 23.05.2013 therefore, neither
the mistake of the Hon'ble Court nor the mistake of
the counsel of the appellants as the counsel of the
appellants was not aware about the death of the
respondent no. 1 therefore, the judgment on merit
cannot be recalled.
(iii) It is settled law that inherent powers can be exercised
by the Court to do substantial Justice. Prayer for
recall of an order can be made if the applicant shows
that there was a mistake of the Court while passing its
order.
(iv) The applicants did not disclose to come in the Court
and to move the recall application at this juncture
after a lapse of near about 7 months from the date of
order and after a lapse of 6 years from the date of
death alleged by them.
(v) In case the applicants do not succeed in the recall
application, he can take the benefit of the legal
consequences of the judgment dated 23.05.2013
which is always open for them.
(vi) In the above circumstances, the recall application is
devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed with cost.
3. Whereas the contention of learned Senior Counsel for the
recall applicant is that the order passed by the Co-ordinate Bench
of this Court on 23.05.2013 in Second Appeal is a decree against
dead person, it is the submission of learned Senior counsel for
the appellants that it was the duty of the learned counsel
representing respondent no. 1 to have disclosed the death of his
client to the Court.
4. Order 22 Rule 10A CPC provides as under:
10A. Duty of pleader to communicate to Court
death of a party.-Whenever a pleader appearing for a
party to the suit comes to know of the death of that party,
he shall inform the Court about it, and the Court shall

-4-
thereupon give notice of such death to the other party,
and, for this purpose, the contract between the pleader
and the deceased party shall be deemed to subsist.]
5. It was, therefore, the duty of the pleader representing
respondent no. 1 to have disclosed the death of respondent no. 1
to the Court.
6. It was held in Ghanshyam Raj Narain Dubey vs.
Union of India and Others, 1997 (3) AWC 2.260 (NOC)
as follows:
"It is a settled law that inherent powers can be exercised
by the Court to do substantial justice. There is a difference
between "Recall" and "Restoration". Prayer for Recall of
an order can be made if the applicant shows that there
was a mistake of the Court while passing its order. While
making a prayer for restoration, the applicant must show
the sufficiency of cause of his default and the Cout may
exercise its discretion in accepting that cause. In the
former, the Court has to invoke the doctrine 'Actus Curie
Neminem Gravabit (Act of Court prejudices none),
whereas in the latter, the defaulting party has to show the
bona fides and failure of justice."
7. Learned counsel for the recall applicant referred to a
decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Budhia Swain and
Others vs. Gopinath Deb and Others, (1999) 4 SCC 396,
para 8 of which is being reproduced herein below for
convenience:
(i) the proceedings culminating into an order suffer
from the inherent lack of jurisdiction and such lack of
jurisdiction is patent,
(ii) there exists fraud or collusion in obtaining the
judgment,

-5-
(iii) there has been a mistake of the court prejudicing
a party, or
(iv) a judgment was rendered in ignorance of the
fact that a necessary party had not been served at all or
had died and the estate was not represented.
8. Since none of the above grounds are available to the recall
applicant, therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court,
Bhudia Swain's case (Supra) is not applicable to the facts of
the instant case.
9. Recall application thus fails and is dismissed.
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.)
Dated 15th Sep, 2015
SH
